'''Khash''' ({{langx|hy|խաշ}}) is a traditional dish made from a boiled cow or sheep parts, which might include the head, feet, and stomach ([[tripe]]). It originates from [[Armenia]] and is considered one of the oldest [[Armenian cuisine|Armenian dishes]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The Ethnic Cuisines of our Peoples|publisher=Light and Food Industry|date=1978|language=ru|author=[[William Pokhlyobkin]]|quote=Хаш - одно из древнейших армянских блюд, получивших распространение по всему Закавказью. С древности сохранился обычай есть хаш совершенно отдельно от всех иных блюд, причем рано утром на завтрак или даже до завтрака, по праздничным дням.}}</ref><ref name="Adjarian2">{{cite web |author=Adjarian, Hrachia |author-link=Hrachia Adjarian |year=1973 |title=Armenian Etymological Dictionary |url=http://www.nayiri.com/imagedDictionaryBrowser.jsp?dictionaryId=7&pageNumber=1051 |page=346 |language=hy |volume=2}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Heratsi |first=Mkhitar |title=Relief Of Fevers |year=1178 |isbn=978-0-8134-3032-4 |pages=Chapter 6 and Chapter 10|publisher=Interstate Publishers }}</ref> 
	
In addition to Armenia, khash and its variations are also found in several other countries, including [[Afghanistan]], [[Albania]], [[Azerbaijan]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Bulgaria]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Greece]], [[Iran]], [[Iraq]], [[Mongolia]], [[North Macedonia]], [[Turkey]], and some [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Persian Gulf countries]].
